title: Memory-adaptive KV downshift and async-restore protocol for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We observe intermittent GPU OOMs in production during heavy continuous-batching workloads where long KV contexts (multi-turn chat + embeddings) plus aggressive prefetch spikes memory usage. Existing reactions (hard eviction or full model fallback) are either too disruptive or too late. This work implements a memory-adaptive "downshift" protocol that intentionally degrades KV representation and admission behavior before OOM, plus an async restore pipeline to recover trimmed KV without blocking user requests.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce production OOM events caused by KV + batch spikes by >= 80% on the pilot cluster
95th percentile request success (no hard fallback) maintained at >= 99% during controlled spike tests
Fallback to quantized/minimal model for affected requests occurs < 5% of the time under normal load and is fully audited
New metrics exposed in Console: kv_downshift_rate, kv_restoration_time, slot_memory_headroom, admission_retries
End-to-end integration tests and chaos scenarios added to CI that reproduce OOM conditions and validate graceful degradation and recovery
tasks: Write design doc: "Memory-adaptive downshift and async-restore" (include cost model and heuristics)
Prototype admission controller that computes per-slot memory budget and issues shrink/compact decisions
Implement compact-kv representation (lossy compression + token-header caching) and spill-to-host path
Build async restore agent: background thread that rehydrates trimmed KV from persistent or remote cache
Add admission retry + jittered exponential backoff and request-level metadata for observability
Unit tests for compaction correctness and KV consistency guarantees
Integration load test harness that simulates long-context chat + streaming to trigger downshift
Create Console dashboards and alerts for new metrics
Canary rollout plan and rollback hooks
technical_notes: Admission: on request enqueue compute expected incremental GPU bytes = prefix_kv_estimate(request) + token_estimate(batch)
Downshift tiers: (1) header-only KV (ids + token counts), (2) compacted embeddings (8-bit lossy), (3) spill-to-host pageable slices
Prioritization: requests tagged by customer_tier and latency_slo; prefer compaction over model fallback for P1/P2 customers
Async restore: maintain per-slot restore queue with rate limiter; restoration is incremental and cooperative with batching to avoid bursts
Consistency: trimmed KV includes a short hash and sequence number; rehydration validates and invalidates partial caches on mismatch
Fallback strategy: if memory headroom < safety_threshold after downshift attempt, fallback to compatible smaller model variant with same API semantics
Metrics: track pre_downshift_memory, post_downshift_memory, restoration_latency_ms, compaction_ratio
Kernel/cuda notes: prefer fused attention kernel with reduced workspace when compacted sequences are used; coordinate with kernel selection module to avoid high-temp allocations
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - internal dev cluster: unit + smoke tests (1 day)
Stage 1 - canary on non-critical shard (5% traffic, 48h monitoring)
Stage 2 - broader pilot across 10% of production shards (72h, run load tests in parallel)
Stage 3 - progressive ramp to 25% then 60% with automatic rollback on OOM/regression alerts
Stage 4 - full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics and post-mortem review
test_plan: Synthetic spike test: simultaneous long-context requests + large batch admissions to verify downshift triggers before OOM
Chaos test: force GPU malloc failure paths to validate retry and fallback behavior
Regression test: ensure no user-visible token corruption after compaction/restore
Load test: steady-state throughput with intermittent heavy requests to measure tail latencies and compaction frequency
A/B: compare cost per token and latency with and without downshift under matched workloads
